Container.Name: Sleutharr
Container.Overview:
Sleutharr answers one question: "I requested this - where did it die?"
It stitches a single request into one timeline across your request manager, Sonarr/Radarr, your download client and your media server, then tells you where the chain broke and what to do about it.
Supports Seerr, Overseerr, Jellyseerr and Ombi; Sonarr and Radarr (any number of instances, including 4K splits); qBittorrent, Transmission, Deluge, SABnzbd and NZBGet; and Plex, Jellyfin and Emby.
Read-only by default. The one exception is a "remove and blocklist" button for stuck downloads, which always asks for confirmation and never runs automatically.
All service URLs and API keys are configured in the web UI, not through environment variables. Add your services on the Settings page after first start, then press "Find my other services" and Sleutharr will read the rest of your setup for you.
Container.Description:
The *arr stack is very good at each individual job and gives you nothing that spans them. When a request never arrives, the answer is somewhere across five different web UIs, and the symptom rarely matches the cause:
• Sonarr says "no results" - because the item is not monitored. • The download client shows 100% - because the import failed on a hardlink error. • The *arr says "imported" - because Plex mounts that folder at a different path.
Sleutharr gives you a single verdict per request, the evidence behind it, and the specific next action - with a link straight to the record in whichever app owns the fix.
**Setting it up**
Add your request manager, then press "Find my other services". Sleutharr reads your Sonarr and Radarr instances out of it - including the two settings that are easy to get wrong by hand - and then reads your download clients out of those. For Plex you sign in with your Plex account and pick a server; there is no token to hunt down.
**What it can fix for you**
Every action asks first and nothing runs unattended:
• Remove a stuck download and blocklist the release, so the *arr finds another. • Retry a request whose hand-off to Sonarr/Radarr failed. • Add the folder mapping when your media server sees files at a different path. • Ask your indexers why nothing is being grabbed, and show the exact reason each release was rejected.
Container.DonateText: If Sleutharr saved you some time, buy me a coffee.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the Sleutharr web interface.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Holds the SQLite database, the generated secret key, and logs.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID that owns files written to /config.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID that owns files written to /config.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Timezone, e.g. Europe/London. Affects displayed timestamps.

Config.Name: CSRF trusted origins
Config.Description: Only needed behind an https reverse proxy. Comma-separated, e.g. https://sleutharr.example.com
